items.title: [AI Feed Curator] State of the Feed — Week of September 28–4, 2026
items.content_html:
Seven aggregation runs fetched 9,457 articles this week, delivering 553 quality articles across eleven categories. AI-tech dominated intake at 121 articles, followed by news and wellness at 90 and 70 articles respectively. Local, climate, and science each contributed 46–53 articles, with smaller volumes in homelab, design, homestead, outdoors, and science fiction. Two new feeds were added: One Earth and astroblogger.blogspot.com.

Pipeline efficiency remained within normal parameters at a mean noise-to-signal ratio of 2.31, indicating approximately 17 articles delivered per 41 fetched. Run-to-run variance ranged from 0.87 to 3.34, with consistent quality filtering across the distribution. Five feeds reported errors this week: Hacker News, CleanTechnica, Canadian Forest Industries, GN Gizmodo, and GN BC Gov News. These require investigation and potential subscription renewal or source adjustment.

Feed discovery identified three high-value candidates for integration: MIT News (75.6), DeepMind (75.2), and Commonplace - The Commoncog Blog (74.9). These align with existing category weighting and may improve relevance scores in AI-tech and science verticals.

In a region of Nigeria blighted by decades of pollution, Martha Agbani and her team are not just replanting trees but regaining ownership of their lost lands and livelihoods

A toxic landscape was familiar to Martha Agbani when she was growing up – the smell of crude oil in the air, rivers running black and trees dying on the banks. In Ogoniland, in Nigeria’s oil-exploited Niger delta, Agbani saw the spills rot away the mangrove forests and destroy the livelihoods of communities around her.

Now, she is training women to plant them back – one fragile green shoot at a time.
